paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: In this task, you are to write an essay on the role of physical exercise in achieving success at college. You will have 30 minutes for the task. You should write at least 120 words but no more than 180 words.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：在本任务中，您将写一篇关于体育锻炼在大学取得成功中的作用的文章。您将有 30 分钟的时间来完成该任务。您应该写至少 120 个字但不超过 180 个字。

paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: In this section, you will hear three news reports. At the end of each news report, you will hear two or three questions. Both the news report and the questions will be spoken only once. After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A), B), C) and D). Then mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 1 with a singles line through the centre.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明： 在本节中，您将听到三则新闻报道。在每篇新闻报道的最后，你都会听到两到三个问题。新闻报道和提问均只发言一次。听到问题后，您必须从标有 A)、B)、C) 和 D) 的四个选项中选择最佳答案。然后在答题卡 1 上用一条穿过中心的单线标记相应的字母。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 1 and 2 are based on the news report you have just heard.
paragraphs.translationZh: 问题1和2是根据你刚才听到的新闻报道得出的。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 3 and 4 are based on the news report you have just heard.
paragraphs.translationZh: 问题3和4是根据你刚才听到的新闻报道提出的。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 5 to 7 are based on the news report you have just heard.
paragraphs.translationZh: 问题5至7是根据你刚才听到的新闻报道得出的。

Then mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 1 with a single line through the centre.

paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: In this section, there is a passage with ten blanks. You are required to select one word for each blank from a list of choices given in a word bank following the passage. Read the passage through carefully before making your choices. Each choice in the bank is identified by a letter. Please mark the corresponding letter for each item on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre. You may not use any of the words in the bank more than once.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：在本节中，有一段有十个空格。您需要从文章后面的单词库中给出的选项列表中为每个空白选择一个单词。在做出选择之前仔细阅读该段落。银行中的每个选择都由一个字母标识。请在答题卡 2 上的每个项目上用一条穿过中心的单线标记相应的字母。您不得多次使用银行中的任何单词。

paragraphs.sourceText: Researchers, writing in the journal Heart, pooled data from 23 studies and found that social isolation or feelings of loneliness were tied to an increased risk of coronary heart disease (冠心病) and strokes.
paragraphs.translationZh: 研究人员在《Heart》杂志上撰文，汇总了 23 项研究的数据，发现社会孤立或孤独感与冠心病和中风的风险增加有关。

paragraphs.sourceText: The studies included data from 181,006 men and women ages 18 and over. There were 4,628 coronary events and 3,002 strokes in follow-up periods 26 from three to 21 years. Three of the papers 27 loneliness, 18 looked at social isolation and two included both. Social isolation and loneliness were determined with questionnaires; the researchers depended on medical records and death 28 for determining coronary events and strokes.
paragraphs.translationZh: 这些研究纳入了 181,006 名 18 岁及以上男性和女性的数据。在 3 至 21 年的随访期内，共有 4,628 例冠状动脉事件和 3,002 例中风。其中 3 篇论文测量了孤独感，18 篇论文研究了社会孤立性，还有 2 篇论文同时涵盖了两者。通过问卷调查确定社会孤立和孤独感；研究人员依靠医疗记录和死亡证明来确定冠状动脉事件和中风。

paragraphs.sourceText: The scientists found that loneliness and social isolation increased the 29 risk of having a heart attack or a death from heart disease by 29 percent, and the risk of stroke by 32 percent. There were no 30 between men and women.
paragraphs.translationZh: 科学家发现，孤独和社会孤立使心脏病发作或死于心脏病的相对风险增加 29%，中风的风险增加 32%。男性和女性之间没有差异。

paragraphs.sourceText: "People have tended to focus from a policy point of view on 31 lonely people to make them more 32 ," said the lead author, Nicole K. Valtorta, a research fellow at the University of York in England. "Our study 33 that if this is a risk factor, then we should be trying to prevent the risk factor in the first place."
paragraphs.translationZh: 该研究的主要作者、英国约克大学研究员妮可·K·瓦尔托塔 (Nicole K. Valtorta) 表示：“从政策角度来看，人们倾向于关注孤独的人，让他们的联系更加紧密。” “我们的研究表明，如果这是一个风险因素，那么我们应该首先努力预防该风险因素。”

paragraphs.sourceText: The authors 34 that this was a review of observational studies and did not 35 cause and effect.
paragraphs.translationZh: 作者承认这是对观察性研究的回顾，并未确定因果关系。

paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: In this section, you are going to read a passage with ten statements attached to it. Each statement contains information given in one of the paragraphs. Identify the paragraph from which the information is derived. You may choose a paragraph more than once. Each paragraph is marked with a letter. Answer the questions by marking the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：在本节中，您将阅读一段附有十个陈述的段落。每条陈述都包含其中一个段落中给出的信息。确定信息来源的段落。您可以多次选择一个段落。每个段落都标有一个字母。通过在答题卡 2 上标记相应的字母来回答问题。

paragraphs.sourceText: The hidden costs colleges don't want you to know about
paragraphs.translationZh: 大学不想让你知道的隐性成本

paragraphs.sourceText: A) This fall, thousands of college students from across the country will begin their undergraduate studies at colleges around the nation. They will inevitably pack too much to fit in their tiny dorm rooms. They will also carry with them a huge student loan debt, in addition to countless "hidden" out-of-pocket costs paid for by their bank accounts and the bank accounts of their families.
paragraphs.translationZh: A) 今年秋天，来自全国各地的数千名大学生将在全国各地的大学开始本科学习。他们不可避免地会带太多东西，无法装进狭小的宿舍。他们还将背负巨额学生贷款债务，此外还有无数由他们的银行账户和家庭银行账户支付的“隐性”自付费用。

paragraphs.sourceText: B) At my well-respected, private, four-year university in Washington, D.C., which boasts a yearly tuition of $44,046 not including room and board, I receive over $57,000 yearly in financial aid. As a student from a family that is struggling to make ends meet, my financial aid package is a combination of federal grants and federal work study, university merit scholarships and financial aid awards, and about $8,000 yearly in federally subsidized (有补贴的) and unsubsidized loans. On paper, my expenses and my financial aid just about even out. Off paper, they don't.
paragraphs.translationZh: B) 在我位于华盛顿特区的备受尊敬的私立四年制大学，每年学费为 44,046 美元（不包括食宿），我每年收到超过 57,000 美元的经济援助。作为一名来自一个入不敷出的家庭的学生，我的经济援助计划包括联邦助学金和联邦勤工俭学、大学优秀奖学金和经济援助奖，以及每年约 8,000 美元的联邦补贴和无补贴贷款。从账面上看，我的开支和经济援助几乎持平。从纸上看，他们没有。

paragraphs.sourceText: C) Universities today are in the business of making money, and mine is no exception. They hit me right out of gate with a $160 fee to attend my freshman orientation, a price which does not include the cost of travel to and from the District. Almost every class has an associated fee not included in the cost of tuition, most between $40 and $100. Fees for lab science classes are the highest, and all students at my university are required to take at least one lab before they graduate. Buying a laptop proved a necessity and, thankfully, a relative bought me one as a gift. Renting a mini-fridge for my dorm room costs my roommates and me about $140 a year.
paragraphs.translationZh: C) 如今的大学都是为了赚钱，我的大学也不例外。他们一出门就给了我 160 美元的费用，让我参加我的新生入学培训，这个价格不包括往返学区的交通费用。几乎每个课程都有不包含在学费中的相关费用，大多数在 40 美元到 100 美元之间。实验科学课程的费用是最高的，我大学的所有学生在毕业前都必须至少参加一门实验。事实证明，购买一台笔记本电脑是必需的，值得庆幸的是，一位亲戚给我买了一台作为礼物。我和我的室友每年为宿舍租一台迷你冰箱的费用约为 140 美元。

paragraphs.sourceText: D) Schools will charge you whatever they can. The costs of any damage to the dorm, including elevators, bathrooms, and common areas, are billed to every person on a dorm floor, or even the entire building if they do not know who caused the damage. After I fell out of my bed twice during my freshman year, the university installed a railing — for $20, billed to my student account. My financial aid did not anticipate any of these costs, and so it did not cover them.
paragraphs.translationZh: D) 学校会尽可能向您收取费用。对宿舍（包括电梯、浴室和公共区域）造成任何损坏的费用将由宿舍楼层的每个人承担，如果他们不知道是谁造成了损坏，甚至是整栋大楼的费用。在我大一的时候从床上摔下来两次后，学校安装了一个栏杆——花费了 20 美元，记入我的学生账户。我的经济援助没有预见到任何这些费用，因此它不包括这些费用。

paragraphs.sourceText: E) An Internet search of "hidden costs" of college turns up a host of articles on parent-centered websites on the college application process. These articles are almost always geared towards upper- and middle- class families. For students already struggling to pay tuition, these costs may be the least of their worries.
paragraphs.translationZh: E) 在互联网上搜索大学的“隐性成本”，会发现以家长为中心的网站上有大量关于大学申请过程的文章。这些文章几乎总是针对中上层阶级家庭。对于已经难以支付学费的学生来说，这些费用可能是他们最不担心的。

paragraphs.sourceText: F) So what hidden costs should low-income students really be paying attention to? My college experience offers a few examples.
paragraphs.translationZh: F) 那么低收入学生应该真正关注哪些隐性成本？我的大学经历提供了一些例子。

paragraphs.sourceText: G) If you are a low-income student who will be attending school out-of-state, make sure you know if you can use your state benefits, such as the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program, or SNAP. It wasn't until after I had accepted admission to an out-of-state school that I learned that I could not use my Ohio Medicaid on campus for anything other than emergency care. My benefits became invalid the second I moved out of Ohio. After my freshman year, I had to opt for the school's insurance plan, which costs around $2,000 a year. Even if your school offers a flat-rate fee for a doctor's appointment at the student health center (mine is $20 a visit), these fees often do not include extra fees for lab tests or prescription medications (药物) .
paragraphs.translationZh: G) 如果您是一名将在州外上学的低收入学生，请确保您知道您是否可以使用州福利，例如补充营养援助计划 (SNAP)。直到我接受一所州外学校的录取后，我才知道除了紧急护理之外，我不能在校园内使用俄亥俄州医疗补助计划进行任何其他活动。我搬出俄亥俄州后，我的福利就失效了。大一结束后，我不得不选择学校的保险计划，每年费用约为 2,000 美元。即使您的学校为学生健康中心的医生预约提供固定费率（我的是每次 20 美元），这些费用通常不包括实验室测试或处方药 (药物) 的额外费用。

paragraphs.sourceText: H) If you plan on paying off bills in your student account with a credit card, be aware of any additional costs. My school charges an additional fee for the use of a credit card to settle outstanding charges, which can add upwards of 3% of the balance to your bill.
paragraphs.translationZh: H) 如果您计划使用信用卡偿还学生帐户中的账单，请注意任何额外费用。我的学校对使用信用卡结算未付费用收取额外费用，这可能会增加您帐单余额的 3% 以上。

paragraphs.sourceText: I) There is another depressing reality hidden within even the largest financial aid packages: Colleges often offer the most generous packages during freshman year as a way to attract new students. My family was careful to ask about the chances of financial aid being taken away after my freshman year. We were assured that, except for low grades or a raise in family income, no money would be taken away. We did not know to ask — and the school did not readily point out — that even if tuition rises, my financial aid package will stay the same. So when my university voted to raise tuition costs 3% at the end of my freshman year, my financial aid package remained the same and I was suddenly responsible for an additional $1,200 for the next year. The university administration will likely vote to raise costs at least once more before my graduation.
paragraphs.translationZh: I）即使是最大的经济援助方案中也隐藏着另一个令人沮丧的现实：大学通常在新生期间提供最慷慨的方案作为吸引新生的一种方式。我的家人小心翼翼地询问我大一后经济援助被取消的可能性。我们被保证，除了成绩低或家庭收入增加之外，不会拿走任何钱。我们不知道要问——学校也没有轻易指出——即使学费上涨，我的经济援助计划也将保持不变。因此，当我的大学在我大一结束时投票决定将学费提高 3% 时，我的经济援助计划保持不变，我突然要为下一年额外支付 1,200 美元。在我毕业之前，大学管理层可能会投票至少再次提高费用。

paragraphs.sourceText: J) Yes, I chose to attend an expensive university far from my hometown. Yes, there were cheaper options. But there are promising students from struggling families across the nation who should not rule out their dream schools entirely. All things considered, I am paying significantly less than the ticket price of my university, and having an educational experience in Washington, D.C., that I would not have had anywhere else. As a low-income student from a down-and-out Rust Belt community, these educational experiences have enormous potential to brighten my future — and my family's future.
paragraphs.translationZh: J) 是的，我选择去一所远离家乡的昂贵大学。是的，还有更便宜的选择。但全国各地都有来自贫困家庭的有前途的学生，他们不应该完全排除他们梦想的学校。考虑到所有因素，我支付的费用远远低于我的大学门票价格，并且在华盛顿特区获得了我在其他地方无法获得的教育经历。作为一名来自贫困铁锈地带社区的低收入学生，这些教育经历具有巨大的潜力，可以照亮我和我家人的未来。

paragraphs.sourceText: K) The key is to make sure that students and their families understand that hidden costs exist, and that they may prove problematic. Fill out a more comprehensive checklist, and be wary of listed prices that seem too low. Understand just how complicated the financial aid process is.
paragraphs.translationZh: K) 关键是要确保学生及其家人了解隐藏成本的存在，并且这些成本可能会带来问题。填写更全面的清单，并警惕看起来太低的标价。了解经济援助流程有多么复杂。

paragraphs.sourceText: L) Students and families must also understand their ability to self-advocate. They should not pay student bills or excess fees blindly. If something does not look right, ask about it. If it still doesn't look right, negotiate it. In cases where parents are working multiple jobs, are less knowledgeable about college bureaucracies, have limited English language skills, or are not contributing financially to their child's education, the burden of self-advocacy will fall on the student. I understand the difficulty, and the embarrassment. But it is necessary.
paragraphs.translationZh: L) 学生和家庭还必须了解他们自我倡导的能力。他们不应该盲目支付学生账单或超额费用。如果有什么事情看起来不对劲，请询问。如果看起来仍然不合适，请协商。如果父母身兼数职，对大学官僚机构了解较少，英语语言技能有限，或者没有为孩子的教育提供经济资助，那么自我宣传的负担就会落在学生身上。我理解其中的困难和尴尬。但这是必要的。

paragraphs.sourceText: M) In the grand scheme of things, however, colleges also must come to understand that the hidden fees they ask for may prove unmanageable for the very kinds of low-income or first-generation students they are trying desperately to attract.
paragraphs.translationZh: M）然而，从长远来看，大学也必须明白，他们要求的隐性费用对于他们拼命吸引的低收入或第一代学生来说可能是难以管理的。

paragraphs.sourceText: 36. Students' financial aid remains unchanged even when tuition rises.
paragraphs.translationZh: 36. 即使学费上涨，学生的经济援助也保持不变。

paragraphs.sourceText: 37. Students may not be able to enjoy their state benefits when they go to college out of the state.
paragraphs.translationZh: 37. 学生在州外上大学时可能无法享受州福利。

paragraphs.sourceText: 38. The financial aid the author receives is supposed to cover all her college expenses.
paragraphs.translationZh: 38. 提交人收到的经济援助应足以支付她的所有大学费用。

paragraphs.sourceText: 39. When the person who damages dorm facilities is not identified, students are required to share the cost.
paragraphs.translationZh: 39. 如果损坏宿舍设施的人身份不明，学生必须分担费用。

paragraphs.sourceText: 40. Though it is difficult and embarrassing, students should make inquiries about what fees they have to pay and why.
paragraphs.translationZh: 40. 虽然这很困难和尴尬，但学生应该询问他们必须支付哪些费用以及为什么。

paragraphs.sourceText: 41. Today, many Americans have to go to college on student loans.
paragraphs.translationZh: 41. 如今，许多美国人必须靠学生贷款上大学。

paragraphs.sourceText: 42. Receiving education in a private university in the nation's capital may change the author's future life and that of her family's.
paragraphs.translationZh: 42. 在国家首都的一所私立大学接受教育可能会改变提交人及其家人的未来生活。

paragraphs.sourceText: 43. Students may no longer be qualified for financial aid if they perform poorly in school or if their family income has increased.
paragraphs.translationZh: 43. 如果学生在学校表现不佳或家庭收入增加，他们可能不再有资格获得经济援助。

paragraphs.sourceText: 44. In addition to tuition, college students have to pay extra fees for the courses they take.
paragraphs.translationZh: 44. 除了学费之外，大学生还必须为他们所修的课程支付额外的费用。

paragraphs.sourceText: 45. Some schools charge students a fee to their student accounts for using credit cards to pay bills.
paragraphs.translationZh: 45. 一些学校向学生收取使用信用卡支付账单的费用。

paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: There are 2 passages in this section. Each passage is followed by some questions or unfinished statements. For each of them there are four choices marked A), B), C) and D). You should decide on the best choice and mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：本节有 2 段。每段文章后面都有一些问题或未完成的陈述。每个选项都有四个选项，标记为 A)、B)、C) 和 D)。您应该决定最佳选择，并在答题卡 2 上用一条穿过中心的单线标记相应的字母。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 46 to 50 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 46 至 50 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: To write his 2010 book, The 5-Factor World Diet, nutritionist Harley Pasternak traveled to the healthiest countries around the world to learn more about what made their meals extra nourishing.
paragraphs.translationZh: 为了撰写 2010 年的著作《世界五要素饮食》，营养学家哈雷·帕斯捷尔纳克 (Harley Pasternak) 走访了世界上最健康的国家，以了解更多关于如何让他们的膳食变得更加营养的信息。

paragraphs.sourceText: He noted that Japanese people ate a wonderful variety of seaweeds, and that Chinese people tried to include at least five different colors in every meal. Pasternak also came away with some valuable observations about how different the North American way of life was, compared with many other countries.
paragraphs.translationZh: 他指出，日本人吃的海藻种类繁多，而中国人试图在每顿饭中至少加入五种不同颜色的海藻。帕斯捷尔纳克还对北美生活方式与许多其他国家相比有多么不同提出了一些有价值的观察。

paragraphs.sourceText: For starters, Americans eat much bigger portions than people in other countries. "We don't prioritize eating seasonally or locally, and we also add lots of salt, sugar and thickening agents to our foods," explained Pasternak. Contrast that to the healthy Mediterranean, Nordic and Okinawan diets listed in Pasternak's book. They all seem to stick to the ethos (特质) of regional, seasonal produce.
paragraphs.translationZh: 首先，美国人吃的食物比其他国家的人多得多。帕斯捷尔纳克解释说：“我们并不优先考虑季节性或当地的饮食，我们还在食物中添加大量的盐、糖和增稠剂。”与帕斯捷尔纳克书中列出的健康地中海、北欧和冲绳饮食进行对比。他们似乎都坚持地区季节性产品的民族精神。

paragraphs.sourceText: For example, a traditional Mediterranean diet includes fruits, vegetables, whole grains, nuts and olive oil as the main components of nutritional intake. Fish, chicken and red wine make moderate appearances, while red meat, salt and sugar are used much less often. The benefits of a traditional Mediterranean diet have been studied since the 1970s, and researchers have found that living that olive oil life can help people lose weight, lower their heart disease risk and reverse diabetes.
paragraphs.translationZh: 例如，传统的地中海饮食包括水果、蔬菜、全谷物、坚果和橄榄油作为营养摄入的主要成分。鱼、鸡肉和红酒的用量适中，而红肉、盐和糖的用量要少得多。自 20 世纪 70 年代以来，人们就开始研究传统地中海饮食的好处，研究人员发现，食用橄榄油的生活可以帮助人们减肥、降低心脏病风险并逆转糖尿病。

paragraphs.sourceText: Most other healthy eating cultures also make meals an event — say, multiple courses around the family table, or a glass or two of red wine at a long lunch — as opposed to hastily wolfing down handfuls of cereal above the kitchen sink and calling it dinner.
paragraphs.translationZh: 大多数其他健康饮食文化也将进餐视为一件大事——比如，在家庭餐桌上吃几道菜，或者在一顿丰盛的午餐中喝一两杯红酒——而不是在厨房水槽上匆匆狼吞虎咽地吃下一把麦片，然后称之为晚餐。

paragraphs.sourceText: Each of the healthy eating cultures has its own unique feature. But Pasternak did take note of one unifying factor in all of the healthy societies he observed. "The only overlapping feature in most of these healthy countries is that they all walk way more than the average American," said Pasternak. "So really, regardless of what you're eating, if someone's walking four miles more than you each day, they're going to be a lot thinner and live a lot longer than you."
paragraphs.translationZh: 每种健康饮食文化都有其独特的特点。但帕斯捷尔纳克确实注意到了他观察到的所有健康社会中的一个统一因素。帕斯捷尔纳克说：“大多数健康国家的唯一重叠特征是，他们的步行时间都比普通美国人多得多。” “所以说真的，不管你吃什么，如果有人每天比你多走四英里，他们就会比你瘦得多，寿命也长得多。”

paragraphs.sourceText: Recognizing when a friend or colleague feels sad, angry or surprised is key to getting along with others. But a new study suggests that being sensitive to people's feelings may sometimes come with an extra dose of stress. This and other research challenge the prevailing view that emotional intelligence is uniformly beneficial to its bearer.
paragraphs.translationZh: 认识到朋友或同事何时感到悲伤、愤怒或惊讶是与他人相处的关键。但一项新的研究表明，对人们的感受敏感有时可能会带来额外的压力。这项研究和其他研究挑战了流行的观点，即情商对其持有者来说都是有益的。

paragraphs.sourceText: In a study, psychologist Myriam Bechtoldt of the Frankfurt School of Finance and Management in Germany asked 166 male university students a series of questions to measure their emotional intelligence. For example, they showed the students photographs of people's faces and asked them to what extent feelings such as happiness or disgust were being expressed. The students then had to give job talks in front of judges who displayed serious facial expressions. The scientists measured concentrations of stress hormones in the students' saliva (唾液) before and after the talk.
paragraphs.translationZh: 在一项研究中，德国法兰克福金融与管理学院的心理学家 Myriam Bechtoldt 向 166 名男性大学生提出了一系列问题来衡量他们的情商。例如，他们向学生展示人们脸部的照片，并询问他们在多大程度上表达了诸如快乐或厌恶之类的感受。然后，学生们必须在表情严肃的评委面前进行工作演讲。科学家们在演讲前后测量了学生唾液中压力荷尔蒙的浓度。

paragraphs.sourceText: In students who were rated more emotionally intelligent, the stress measures increased more during the experiment and took longer to go back to baseline. The findings suggest that some people may be too emotionally clever for their own good, says Bechtoldt. "Sometimes you can be so good at something that it causes trouble," she notes.
paragraphs.translationZh: 在被评为情商较高的学生中，实验期间压力测量值增加更多，并且需要更长的时间才能回到基线。贝希托尔特说，研究结果表明，有些人可能在情感上过于聪明，这对他们自己没有好处。 “有时候，你可能在某件事上太擅长，但却会带来麻烦，”她指出。

paragraphs.sourceText: Indeed, the study adds to previous research hinting at a dark side of emotional intelligence. A study published in 2002 in Personality and Individual Differences suggested that emotionally perceptive people might be particularly influenced by feelings of depression and hopelessness. Furthermore, several studies have implied that emotional intelligence can be used to manipulate others for personal gains.
paragraphs.translationZh: 事实上，这项研究补充了之前的研究，暗示了情商的阴暗面。 2002 年发表在《人格与个体差异》杂志上的一项研究表明，情绪敏感的人可能特别容易受到抑郁和绝望感的影响。此外，一些研究表明情商可以用来操纵他人以获取个人利益。

paragraphs.sourceText: More research is needed to see how exactly the relation between emotional intelligence and stress would play out in women and in people of different ages and education levels. Nevertheless, emotional intelligence is a useful skill to have, as long as you learn to also properly cope with emotions—both others' and your own, says Bechtoldt. For example, some sensitive individuals may assume responsibility for other people's sadness or anger, which ultimately stresses them out. Remember, as Bechtoldt says, "you are not responsible for how other people feel."
paragraphs.translationZh: 需要更多的研究来了解情商和压力之间的关系到底如何在女性以及不同年龄和教育水平的人中发挥作用。然而，贝希托尔特说，只要你学会正确应对他人和你自己的情绪，情商就是一项有用的技能。例如，一些敏感的人可能会为其他人的悲伤或愤怒承担责任，这最终会给他们带来压力。请记住，正如贝希托尔特所说，“你不必对其他人的感受负责。”
